cases.rationale: Barrier and tensile-retention intervals both meet their frozen application-specific hard limits.
Contact-angle diagnostic is present and bond outcome is declared successful, but barrier transmission degradation violates the hard upper limit.
Barrier interval overlaps the maximum permitted ratio; uncertainty blocks safe-window admission.
A wettability diagnostic without any hard substrate-integrity measurement cannot qualify a safe process window.
ASTM D882 is not used for film stock at or above 1.0 mm; the audit blocks that method/profile combination.
The tensile method receipt lists specimens absent from its analysis manifest.
Visual inspection and process telemetry do not replace calibrated substrate-property measurements.
Treatment-to-bond interval exceeds the declared application-specific maximum window.
Wettability is diagnostic only; hard barrier and tensile properties meet their limits without requiring a minimum contact angle.
A good bond result cannot offset tensile-property retention below the minimum hard limit.
Matched control and treated specimens use the same independent film-roll clusters while preserving distinct specimen identities.
Independent-arm design reuses a production film roll across baseline and treated arms.
A study plan changed after outcomes were available.
A method result is below the predeclared application confidence requirement.
Analysis result references a different plasma exposure profile.
An unrecognized ISO 15106 edition is not admitted by the versioned method registry.
A thin-film tensile method receipt outside its registered material class is blocked pending an applicability review.
